newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Coles Myer sees no trading improvement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Coles Myer sees no trading improvement.

text.p: Retailer Coles Myer said on Tuesday it does not expect any short term improvement in the difficult retail environment across Australia.

Coles Myer said also that after a strategic review of its World 4 Kids toy chain, it has decided to keep some stand alone World 4 Kids stores. It said it remained committed to the Australian toy and leisure market and would retain the World 4 Kids brand.

"We do not expect any short term improvement in the difficult retail climate across Australia except perhaps in Victoria, where the government's deregulation of trading hours will enable retailers to compete more effectively with other forms of discretionary expenditure," Coles Myer managing director Peter Bartels said in releasing Coles' annual results.

Earlier Coles said it posted a pre-abnormals net profit of A$302 million, down 28.4 percent on the previous year. It posted a net profit of A$280.4 million, down 33.8 percent. It set an unchanged final dividend of 10 cents per share.
Coles said its World 4 Kids (W4K) unit posted a loss before interest and tax of A$35.8 million in the 52 weeks to July 28, compared with a loss of A$33.0 million the previous year.
Sales however rose 7.3 percent to A$97.0 million.
"Following a strategic review of W4K the company remains committed to the Australian toy and leisure market and will retain the W4K brand," Coles said.
"This will include some stand-alone W4K stores," it said, adding W4K's business operations were fully integrated into Coles' K-Mart unit during the last quarter of 1995/96.
"Some stores within the 23-store W4K network will be utilised for other Coles Myer businesses, including Officeworks," Coles said.
"The reutilisation of the stores will take time to complete and some costs may be incurred during the process," it said.
Coles included a A$43.4 million abnormal cost in its 1995/96 accounts from the World 4 Kids restructure.
Coles also said its supermarkets and liquor businesses were performing well and Target, Katies and Officeworks had strong positions in their respective markets.

"Repositioning strategies are being implemented in World 4 Kids, Fosseys, Red Rooster, Kmart and Myer Grace Bros and we are seeing measurable behind the scenes improvements which are, as yet, unreflected in the results," said chief operating officer for business units, Dennis Eck.
Coles' shares closed down two cents at A$4.59 on Monday.
